Entity Framework Core is a translator between C# objects and database rows. SQLite stores the database in one file, so you can learn persistence without first setting up a database server.

How to test this example in Visual Studio

Download the project below, extract it into its own folder, then open StudyLab.csproj. Wait for NuGet restore. Choose Build → Build Solution. For console projects choose Start Without Debugging. For API projects use View → Terminal, make sure the terminal is in the folder containing StudyLab.csproj, then run the command shown in the lesson. Do not paste all files into Program.cs: use the exact file names displayed below.

Install and create the right project

  • Install Visual Studio with ASP.NET and web development and a .NET 10-compatible SDK. For WPF also install .NET desktop development. Check Tools → Get Tools and Features if templates are missing.
  • Create ASP.NET Core Empty for the Minimal API, or ASP.NET Core Web API with Use controllers for a controller project. Select .NET 10. Alternatively open the supplied .csproj to get exactly the lesson files.
  • Use a separate folder for every example. Delete the generated weather sample if it conflicts with the supplied files. Restore NuGet packages before building.
  • In View → Terminal, cd into the folder containing StudyLab.csproj. For local API testing run dotnet run --urls http://localhost:5100. Open requests.http and use Send Request above each request. Use the actual port from the console if you launch with a different profile.

Your first request

GET http://localhost:5100/api/students

Initially expect 200 OK with []. A browser address bar can send GET, but cannot conveniently send all CRUD methods. Use the .http editor, Postman, curl.exe or a Swagger UI. The JSON object is a data packet, not an HTML page.

Libraries and schema setup

Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite is the database provider. Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Design supplies design-time services for migrations. Keep EF packages and dotnet-ef on matching major versions. The project pins package versions in StudyLab.csproj; restore installs them. Built-in System types do not need separate packages. 

dotnet tool install --global dotnet-ef --version 10.0.15
dotnet ef migrations add InitialCreate
dotnet ef database update
dotnet run --urls http://localhost:5100

If dotnet-ef is already installed, use dotnet tool update --global dotnet-ef --version 10.0.15 instead. Run migrations inside the project folder. The supplied project has no initial migration until you generate it.

Follow the data

appsettings.json contains ConnectionStrings:School = Data Source=school.db. AddDbContext registers SchoolDb as scoped. DbSet<Student> represents the table. Add marks a new entity; SaveChangesAsync sends the INSERT. FindAsync reads a key; changing a tracked entity and saving sends an UPDATE. Remove and save sends DELETE. AsNoTracking makes read-only lists cheaper. CancellationToken can cancel work when a request is abandoned.

Expected result

Run the same six CRUD requests. Stop and restart the app without deleting school.db; the rows you kept should remain. GET after DELETE still returns 404. A migration changes schema; ordinary CRUD changes rows. EnsureCreated is a convenient separate demo shortcut, but do not mix it into a migrations-managed database.

Try it yourself

You see “no such table: Students”. What is missing?

Worked answer

Run dotnet ef migrations add InitialCreate and dotnet ef database update from this project directory before starting the API.

Where is school.db?

Worked answer

The relative connection-string path is resolved from the process working directory. Run from a consistent project folder or configure an absolute path.
